There are a lot of docs#cast/ docs#Eq.rec like functions for various definitions in Mathlib: Fin.cast, List.Vector.congr, Graph.copy, SimpleGraph.Walk.copy, Path.cast, Sym.cast, Partition.copy, Finpartition.copy & etc. All of these functions does the same as h ▸ a where h is a proof of equality of something in the type of a. I think this is caused because proving the properties about h ▸ a is currently too finicky without extra tooling/API.

So I would like to ask: shouldn't we try to make h ▸ a better rather than avoid and circumvent it for each definition we formalize? Would people agree that we should maybe replace a number of ad hoc cast functions with docs#Eq.rec or docs#cast once we have a better support?
I have created a draft PR #38742 (Written by Opus, possibly wrong approach) to try to solve at least part of the problem using simproc.
Graph.copy isn't of the same flavor,
In some cases, it's easier to make an expression with a custom cast elaborate.

I agree that currently, creating an ad hoc cast is more convinient. But I am wondering whether people agree that changes should be made to the general cast to make it easy to use, so that ad hoc cast is not the path of least resistance.
Particular pain point I had with cast is addressed in #38742. @Yury G. Kudryashov , do you have a different pain point that is not the one addressed in that PR? I would be happy to have a bash at it.
Do you mean that you prefer that statements of lemmas like docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_take / docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_add_eq use the triangle operator instead?
Or HEq? (like docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_add_heq / docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_add_heq)
One issue with HEq is that f m = f n does not imply m = n. It works for f = Fin, but not for many other constructions.

Snir Broshi said:

Do you mean that you prefer that statements of lemmas like docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_take / docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_add_eq use the triangle operator instead?

Or HEq? (like docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_add_heq / docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.take_add_heq)

HEq and cast is very close to each other by docs#heq_iff_exists_cast_eq. I would prefer either as the universal way to talk about the cast like operation.

an issue with docs#cast is that if your lemma is h : i = j then cast won't let you go from x : Foo i to Foo j, you have to use cast (congrArg Foo h) x which loses information since many tactics won't inspect inside of the proof congrArg Foo h to find h, and Foo i = Foo j is usually strictly weaker and much less useful than i = j

What if we use Eq.rec/ triangle operator? This doesn't seem to suffer from the problem you are mentioning about docs#cast, in that the original i = j is available as the argument for Eq.rec application. Then tactics should be able to tell apart weaker Foo i = Foo j case from i = j case looking at just one level deep.
But the triangle has less knowledge about its expected type, you can't (by simp) ▸ h but you probably can p₁ = p₂.copy (by simp) (by simp)

import Mathlib
variable {G : SimpleGraph ℕ} {u v : ℕ} {p : G.Walk (u + u) (v + v)} {p' : G.Walk (2 * u) (2 * v)}
example : p = p'.copy (by lia) (by lia) := sorry
example : p = (by lia) ▸ (by lia) ▸ p' := sorry -- fails

(the definition of p.copy hu hv is hu ▸ hv ▸ p)
Agreed. In my experience ▸ often needs a lot of type annotation to work
I wonder if we allow the ad hoc copy functions as transparent definition, whether we could have one set of, say simproc, that is capable of simplifying all such functions.
#Is there code for X? > Eq.rec with a constant does nothing: h ▸ c = c some tests for a potential Eq.rec simproc?
Another advantage of customcast operators is that they can have better defeqs; (Fin.cast h x).val = x.val is true by definition, but (_root_.cast (congrArg _ h) x).val = x.val is not.

I'm not sure that having custom cast operators is really that different to having things like docs#Equiv.finsetCongr; if we're going to have functions to cast through equivalences of types, I'm not sure it's worth trying to do something clever for casts along equalities of non-type parameters.

Eric Wieser said:

Another advantage of customcast operators is that they can have better defeqs; (Fin.cast h x).val = x.val is true by definition, but (_root_.cast (congrArg _ h) x).val = x.val is not.

This is the sort of problem #38742 attempts to solve: For any tagged function that extracts data out of a dependent type, f, simproc will simplify f ... (h ▸ x) to f ... x.
It doesn't change defeq.
That is true

Another reason to prefer custom cast operations is that you can write some reliable lemmas that don't rely on higher-order unification that give algebraic properties of the cast (e.g., how do casts commute over various operations?)

A problem with Eq.rec itself is that matching it requires unifying the motive argument, which can be nontrivial, and it easily can fail.

I've had an idea I've been kicking around where you should be able to register custom cast operations with Lean so that it can use them during rewriting, in preference to using Eq.rec itself.

So, I think the matter of extra tooling is that h ▸ a should know about the custom cast operations and use them if possible, rather than simprocs to make specifically simp better at working with Eq.rec.

That said, independent of custom casts, I think your simproc is a great idea to have. Something I would like is if it attempted commuting conversion, rather than just elimination of the recursor. This means transforming f ... (h ▸ x) ... into h' ▸ f ... x ... if possible (which I think simp itself will reduce to f ... x ... if h' could be replaced by rfl).

Unification certainly seems like a problem which also related to the need for more type annotation. I agree that because the custom casts know about the types they are dealing with, they work much more reliably.

This is a slightly different question: if the custom cast functions are just a fact of life, would it be good to have them be auto generated? I am imagining a tag similar to @[simps] in that it auto generates a trivial def/lemma for you that you are gonna need.

Kyle Miller said:

So, I think the matter of extra tooling is that h ▸ a should know about the custom cast operations and use them if possible, rather than simprocs to make specifically simp better at working with Eq.rec.

I think this is a great idea!

Kyle Miller said:

That said, independent of custom casts, I think your simproc is a great idea to have. Something I would like is if it attempted commuting conversion, rather than just elimination of the recursor. This means transforming f ... (h ▸ x) ... into h' ▸ f ... x ... if possible (which I think simp itself will reduce to f ... x ... if h' could be replaced by rfl).

Thank you for your kind words! I will have a look at making it attempt commuting conversion.

Jun Kwon said:

would it be good to have them be auto generated?

Yeah, here's another idea I've been kicking around: there should be a way to generate a map function that gives the functorial structure of a type: each parameter/index of a type can be classified as being fixed, covariant, contravariant, or both, and then you should be able to generate a map function that has a corresponding =, ->, or Equiv for each slot. Then you'd define congr as a specialization of this to = and Equiv, and then, perhaps, cast as a specialization to =. I don't have a clear vision of the interface, and for user-facing cast you'd want to avoid certain rewrites (e.g. it's rare to want to rewrite parameters of a type that are themselves types using =, and more likely an antipattern than not).

The congr definition is something you need to implement a reliable simp_equiv, a tactic that rewrites using equivalences.

Kyle Miller said:

and then you should be able to generate a map function that has a corresponding =, ->, or Equiv for each slot.

Or a LinearEquiv, AlgEquiv, ... ?
Yeah, that's a good direction to generalize, for various simp_linear_equiv, simp_alg_equiv, etc. tactics, for doing rewrites in particular categories of types.
